name: Amantadine

lead: Amantadine began as a flu drug in the 1960s and turned out to help Parkinson's symptoms. Today it is mostly a neurological medicine, including for recovery after brain injury.
People interested in energy and motivation talk about it because it raises dopamine activity, which they connect to training drive.

paras: It increases dopamine release, blocks NMDA glutamate receptors and has mild anticholinergic action. Against flu it blocks the M2 proton channel.

The label lists nausea, dizziness, insomnia, hallucinations, livedo reticularis and low blood pressure on standing. Overdose deaths are documented, especially with kidney impairment. Prescription-only.

angle.text: People discuss amantadine as a dopamine-boosting option for fatigue and motivation, which they link to training consistency and appearance. It is a prescription drug used mainly for Parkinson's disease and brain injury.

lead: Amantadine is an oral prescription drug that increases dopamine signalling and blocks NMDA glutamate receptors. It was first approved in the US in 1966 for influenza A and later became a Parkinson's disease medicine [1][2]. In recovery and focus discussions it is known as a dopaminergic drug that has also been used for brain-injury recovery, fatigue and low motivation, which people connect with energy, training drive and presentation.

The US label lists indications for influenza A prophylaxis and treatment and for parkinsonism and drug-induced extrapyramidal reactions [3]. Because many circulating influenza strains became resistant, antiviral guidance no longer recommends it for flu, and its main role is neurological [4][5]. Extended-release forms were later approved for levodopa-induced dyskinesia [1].

A multicentre randomised trial of 184 patients with severe traumatic brain injury in a vegetative or minimally conscious state reported faster functional recovery on amantadine than placebo over the treatment period [6]. Registered trials have also tested it for post-COVID fatigue and cognition, cerebral palsy and gait in Parkinson's disease [7][8][9][10].
infobox: About 10 to 31 hours; much longer in kidney failure[13]

paras: Against influenza A, amantadine blocks the viral M2 proton channel and so prevents viral uncoating [11][12]. In the nervous system its effects are less fully described and involve enhanced dopamine release, NMDA receptor antagonism and mild anticholinergic action [1].

Wikipedia describes amantadine as a weak NMDA receptor antagonist, a sigma-1 receptor agonist and an agent that promotes dopamine release and blocks its reuptake, while noting that earlier claims of monoamine oxidase inhibition are probably not accurate.[13] It is taken by mouth, is well absorbed (bioavailability 86 to 90 percent), is minimally metabolised, and about 90 percent is excreted unchanged in urine, with a half-life that averages about eight days in end-stage kidney disease.[13] Structural work on the influenza M2 channel it blocks was published in Nature in 2008.[14]

Wikipedia dates the first report of amantadine's antiviral activity to 1963 at the University of Illinois Hospital in Chicago, with first clinical use in West Germany in 1966 and US approval for influenza A prophylaxis in the 1960s.[13][1] The Parkinson's use came from an observation in 1969: a woman with Parkinson's disease who took amantadine for flu reported that her rigidity and tremor eased and returned after the course ended, and later studies supported its use, leading to FDA approval for Parkinson's disease in 1973.[13] Resistance among influenza A strains rose sharply after 2005, with the CDC and WHO now advising against it for influenza A, and Wikipedia cites reports of its use in poultry in China in 2005.[13] Extended-release products for levodopa-induced dyskinesia followed, with Gocovri approved in 2017 according to Grokipedia.[1]

Approved uses are influenza A and parkinsonism [3]. Reviews cover its place among Parkinson's treatments [2] and among options for dementia with Lewy bodies [15]. Systematic reviews of agitation after traumatic brain injury discuss it among the agents studied [16]. Disorders-of-consciousness guidelines address amantadine after brain injury [17].

Beyond labelled indications, the drug is used off-label for fatigue and for recovery after traumatic brain injury. For fatigue in multiple sclerosis, Wikipedia reports that a 2007 Cochrane review found no overall supporting evidence while a 2012 follow-up found possible benefit.[13] For disorders of consciousness, a 2018 American Academy of Neurology guideline recommends considering amantadine in adults 4 to 16 weeks after injury, with long-term benefit unclear.[17][13]

Beyond the 2012 brain-injury trial [6], early reports examined amantadine in depression and migraine in 1971 and 1972 [18][19]. Recent trials include extended-release amantadine for OFF-related dystonia [20] and post-COVID fatigue [10][1].

The 2012 New England Journal of Medicine trial enrolled 184 patients with severe traumatic brain injury in a vegetative or minimally conscious state and reported faster functional recovery on amantadine during the 4-week treatment period.[6] A 2015 meta-analysis considered amantadine among drugs used in Lewy body dementia.[15] Small registered trials cover gait in Parkinson's disease on extended-release amantadine (n=8), long-term effects in dyskinesia (n=80, AMANDYSK), post-COVID cognitive impairment (n=64) and fatigue (n=83), and cerebral palsy (n=11, terminated).[7][8][9][10][21]

The label lists nausea, dizziness and insomnia as most frequent (5-10%), with hallucinations, confusion, livedo reticularis, orthostatic hypotension and others less often [3]. Deaths have been reported from overdose, particularly with kidney impairment [3]. Animal studies showed embryonic toxicity at high doses [3].

Wikipedia lists drowsiness, dizziness, lightheadedness and confusion as common, with dry mouth, constipation and urinary problems from its anticholinergic action, and rare serious effects including neuroleptic malignant syndrome and psychosis. It is contraindicated in end-stage kidney disease, because the drug is cleared by the kidneys, and it can raise serum creatinine.[13] It is prescription-only in the US, Canada, the UK and Australia.[13]

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and focus communities
paras: Amantadine is discussed in nootropic and dopamine-focused circles as a drug that can raise energy, motivation and drive, which proponents connect with showing up to train and keeping up with grooming and presentation. These discussions treat it as a prescription medication, and clinicians describe its established roles as influenza A, Parkinson's disease and dyskinesia, with brain-injury use supported by trial and guideline data.[6][17][3] No published trial has tested it for appearance outcomes or in healthy people seeking motivation; trials of fatigue and cognition are in post-COVID patients.[8][10]

On T Nation, posts mention amantadine in three settings: as an ADHD-adjacent option said to aid executive function, as a dopamine booster one member tried during a testosterone-therapy troubleshooting thread and reported as having no effect for them, and in a list of dopamine-related agents proposed for post-finasteride complaints.[22][23][24] These are individual reports; the drug's label and guideline-supported roles remain those described above.[17][3]

lore.intro: Amantadine appears in a few T Nation threads on ADHD, testosterone-therapy side effects and post-finasteride complaints, where users discuss it as a dopamine-raising option; it is a prescription drug and the posts are individual accounts rather than studies.[22][23][24]
